result.note: Weekly roundup; tested the Centre's telecom and port-clearance decisions and the Russia sanctions and trade facts, skipping the protest item as ephemeral.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about decisions taken by the Centre in September 2026:
items: The validity of environmental clearances for port projects was extended to 10 years.
The inter-ministerial Digital Communications Commission was dissolved.
The change in port clearance validity insulates projects such as Great Nicobar from fresh environmental review.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because port green-clearance validity was doubled to 20 years, not set at 10 years. The dissolution of the Digital Communications Commission hands one desk control over how 1.3 billion users connect.
questions.source: The Centre dissolved the inter-ministerial Digital Communications Commission on Tuesday, handing one desk control of how 1.3 billion users connect, then doubled port green-clearance validity to 20 years on Thursday, insulating slow mega-projects like Great Nicobar from fresh environmental review.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about developments affecting India's external trade in September 2026:
items: A Russia sanctions law signed by US President Trump exposes India to tariffs of up to 100%.
Canada set a December target for concluding its trade pact with India.
India's Russian oil imports rose 16.5% in August 2026.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because India's Russian oil imports fell 16.5% in August, so they were already declining before the sanctions law was signed. Trump signed the law on Monday 21 September 2026.
questions.source: Trump signed the Russia sanctions law exposing India to tariffs up to 100% on Monday, yet India's Russian oil imports were already falling, down 16.5% in August, and Canada set a December target to finish its trade pact.
